issues.legal_issue: A co-owner may obtain a reference for jointly owned acquired property on behalf of the other co-owners, and those co-owners are entitled to enhanced compensation according to their shares when the reference application indicates that they jointly claim higher compensation.
material_facts: The acquired property remained jointly owned by four co-owners after a partition, was managed by one of them, and its income was shared according to their respective shares.
The co-owner who sought references stated that the property belonged to him and his brothers, that they were dissatisfied with the compensation, and that they were entitled to more.

The civil court enhanced the compensation but allocated the enhanced award only to the co-owner who had sought the references, because the other co-owners had not jointly or expressly sought references for every award.
issues.conclusion: The reference application, by necessary implication, sought a reference on behalf of all the co-owners. They were entitled to receive the enhanced compensation pro rata according to their shares.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 4, 9 and 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, when a reference application states that acquired property belongs to the applicant and other co-owners, and that they are dissatisfied and seek higher compensation, it may be understood by necessary implication as seeking a reference on their behalf. A co-owner has an interest in every part of joint property and may act to protect the common property; any compensation is payable pro rata according to the co-owners’ shares. The Court relied on Kanta Goel v. B.P. Pathak, Sri Ram Pasricha v. Jagannath, and Pal Singh v. Sunder Singh.

rule.if: land_acquisition_reference_proceeding and jointly_owned_acquired_property and reference_application_identifies_other_coowners_and_their_joint_dissatisfaction and enhanced_compensation_awarded

predicates.land_acquisition_reference_proceeding: A proceeding seeks a judicial reference concerning compensation for property acquired by the state.
predicates.jointly_owned_acquired_property: The acquired property is owned jointly by multiple people, each with a share in it.
predicates.reference_application_identifies_other_c: The person seeking the reference states that the property belongs to other co-owners as well and that they are dissatisfied with the compensation and seek more.
predicates.enhanced_compensation_awarded: The court awards compensation exceeding the amount previously awarded by the acquiring authority.
predicates.other_coowners_receive_enhanced_compensa: The other co-owners receive the enhanced compensation according to their shares.

issues.definition: When a reference proceeding concerns jointly owned acquired property and the application identifies the other co-owners as jointly dissatisfied with the compensation, an enhanced award is shared with them according to their shares.

issues.legal_issue: The acquiring state cannot defeat co-owners’ entitlement to their proper shares of compensation by relying on technical objections that they did not each expressly seek a reference.
material_facts: The acquiring state argued that co-owners who had not expressly sought references for the relevant awards could not receive enhanced compensation.
The reference application stated that the acquired property belonged to the applicant and his brothers and that they were dissatisfied with the compensation and entitled to more.
The civil court had determined that the co-owners were entitled to shares in the acquired property and had enhanced the compensation.
issues.conclusion: The state had no role in deciding which co-owner was entitled to receive compensation; the court had to award compensation to the rightful persons. The state could contest the amount of compensation, but could not rely on the co-owners’ failure to make separate or express requests to deny their shares.
issues.legal_principle: The state may resist an enhancement and adduce evidence concerning the prevailing market value, but entitlement to compensation as between claimants is for the claimants and the court, not the state. The Court also relied on Ram Kumar v. Union of India for the duty to provide full acquisition information and make a reference, and applied the principles concerning co-owners in Kanta Goel v. B.P. Pathak, Sri Ram Pasricha v. Jagannath, and Pal Singh v. Sunder Singh.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: A proceeding determines compensation for property acquired by the state.
predicates.state_raises_objection_to_coowners_entit: The state argues that some co-owners cannot receive compensation because they did not individually or expressly seek a reference.
predicates.reference_application_indicates_joint_cl: The reference application indicates that the applicant and other co-owners jointly dispute the compensation and seek more.
predicates.coowners_have_shares_in_acquired_propert: The people claiming compensation hold shares in the acquired property.
predicates.state_cannot_deny_coowners_compensation_: The state cannot defeat the co-owners’ entitlement to their respective compensation shares by relying on a technical objection about who sought a reference.

issues.definition: When the state objects to co-owners’ compensation shares based on the absence of individual references, a reference application indicating their joint claim and their shares in the property means the state cannot deny those shares on that technical ground.
